findings.title: Unpinned package executed on every start: @iflow-mcp/super-win-cli-mcp-server
findings.detail: 'iflow-mcp__super-win-cli-mcp-server' launches @iflow-mcp/super-win-cli-mcp-server through npx without a version. The client resolves the version at start time, so any future publish to that package name runs with your credentials. This is how postmark-mcp (Sept 2025) reached roughly 300 organisations.
findings.remediation: Pin an exact version and an integrity hash: "args": ["@iflow-mcp/super-win-cli-mcp-server@<version>"] and drop the -y flag. Re-pin deliberately, after reviewing the diff.

findings.title: Description reads as instructions to the model (p=1.00): execute_command
findings.detail: The description of 'iflow-mcp__super-win-cli-mcp-server.execute_command' scores 1.00 on the instruction-detection model, and carries intent signals: markup_injection. Descriptions are documentation for a human, but they are delivered to the model as trusted context, so text that tells the model what to do is an attack surface rather than a description. The score is driven mainly by: markup_injection, entropy, log_len, imperative_density.

evidence.description:
Execute a command in the specified shell (powershell, cmd, or gitbash)

Example usage (PowerShell):
```json
{
  "shell": "powershell",
  "command": "Get-Process | Select-Object -First 5",
  "workingDir": "C:\Users\username"
}
```

Example usage (CMD):
```json
{
  "shell": "cmd",
  "command": "dir /b",
  "workingDir": "C:\Projects"
}
```

Example usage (Git Bash):
```json
{
  "shell": "gitbash",
  "command": "ls -la",
  "workingDir": "/c/Users/username"
}
```

findings.remediation: Read the description against what the tool actually does. If the text is legitimate, it usually means the tool should not have to instruct the model at all - move the guidance into the parameter descriptions or the server's own docs.

Get the history of executed commands

Example usage:
```json
{
  "limit": 5
}
```

```json
  {
    "command": "Get-Process",
    "output": "...",
    "timestamp": "2024-03-20T10:30:00Z",
    "exitCode": 0
  }
]
```

findings.title: No baseline supplied - drift detection is disabled
findings.detail: Without an approved snapshot the scanner cannot tell a tool that has always been there from one that appeared yesterday. The single most effective MCP control is the diff, and it needs a baseline to diff against.
findings.remediation: Run 'mcp-scrutiny baseline --config <file> --out mcp-baseline.json', commit the file, and pass it back with --baseline on every later scan.
